channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Trains State Officials on Cybersecurity Incident Response
item.description: A national cybersecurity training course was held in Tajikistan from September 21-23, 2026. The event aimed to enhance government bodies' readiness to detect, analyze, and respond to cyber incidents, improving specialists' skills and interagency cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Banking Union Head Supports President's Stance on Unilateral Sanctions
item.description: The president of Kyrgyzstan's Banking Union, Anvar Abdraev, stated that unilateral sanctions hinder small countries' economic development and international relations. He supports President Sadyr Japarov's call for sanctions to be imposed only by UN decisions, calling them a tool of pressure.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Claims Ministry Ignores Smog from Factories
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan alleges the Ministry of Natural Resources is ignoring smog emissions from several factories. The MP cited concerns over the Kant cement and slate plant and three brick factories in Orok, stating Bishkek is surrounded by pollution.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches 206 Investment Projects Worth $9.4 Billion in Andijan Region
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended a ceremony to launch new investment projects in Andijan region. A total of 206 projects valued at $9.4 billion were covered, with 98 projects worth $2.05 billion already launched and construction started on 108 projects worth $7.35 billion. These initiatives span energy, manufacturing, education, and tourism sectors.

item.title: Tajikistan's Manufacturing Industry Output Reached 34.7 Billion Somoni
item.description: The output of Tajikistan's manufacturing industry increased from 19.1 billion to 34.7 billion somoni between 2020 and 2025, nearly doubling. Food production and metallurgy were the largest contributors in 2025. The statistical agency reported these figures.

item.title: Uzbekistan Hero Parda Ziyatov dies at 79
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev expressed condolences on the passing of Parda Ziyatov, a distinguished farmer and Hero of Uzbekistan, who died at 79. Ziyatov, born in 1947, dedicated his life to agricultural development and served as a deputy in the Oliy Majlis.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet Chairman visits China for working trip
item.description: Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan, has arrived in Hangzhou, China, for a working visit. The press service of the Cabinet announced his arrival.

item.title: Andijan to implement 206 investment projects worth $9.4 billion
item.description: Andijan region will implement 206 investment projects totaling $9.4 billion. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev launched 98 new projects and initiated the construction of 108 additional facilities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission Approves Campaign Financing Rules
item.description: The Central Election Commission of Kyrgyzstan has approved regulations for the formation and use of election funds by presidential candidates. The rules define procedures for candidates and parties, including opening special bank accounts and paying election deposits. The commission will monitor fund usage, and candidates must submit financial reports.

item.title: Parliament Dismisses Supreme Court Judge A. Mukhamedzhanov Due to Death
item.description: The Parliament of Kyrgyzstan has dismissed Supreme Court judge A. Mukhamedzhanov from his post following his death. The decision was made during a parliamentary session. A parliamentary committee had previously recommended his early dismissal. Mukhamedzhanov passed away on July 17 at the age of 67 after a prolonged illness.

item.title: Detention Extended for Former Bishkek Security Chief Eldar Zhakypbekov
item.description: The Pervomaisky District Court in Bishkek has extended the detention of Eldar Zhakypbekov, former head of the National Security Committee's department in the capital, until October 15, 2026. Zhakypbekov, nicknamed 'Edu', was arrested on February 15 and is accused of corruption. Three other individuals also had their detention extended.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Over 3 Years for Fighting in Ukraine
item.description: A 26-year-old Uzbek citizen, identified as A.Kh., has been sentenced to three years and one month in prison for fighting on the Russian side in the Ukraine conflict. He reportedly signed a military contract to secure his release from a 12-year sentence for drug trafficking in Russia. He was injured in Ukraine.

item.title: Tajikistan and Grenada Sign Visa-Free Travel Agreement
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin and Grenada's Finance Minister Denis Cornwall met in New York and signed an agreement on mutual visa exemption. The agreement, signed on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly session, allows citizens of both countries to travel visa-free.

item.title: Lithuania Halts Job Applications for Citizens of Central Asian Countries
item.description: Lithuania has stopped accepting job applications from citizens of Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Kazakhstan. The annual quota for workers from third countries was filled in September, leading to the suspension of new applications.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Meets with DFC Head Ben Cardey
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva met with DFC head Ben Cardey in the US. During the meeting, they discussed major joint projects initiated in the transport and healthcare sectors.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Agree on Financial Intelligence Exchange
item.description: Tajikistan and South Korea signed 15 new cooperation documents, including a memorandum on exchanging financial intelligence. The agreement aims to combat money laundering and terrorism financing, fostering mutual cooperation and international interaction.

item.title: Tajikistan and Islamic Development Bank Discuss Energy Investments and Rogun HPP
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Finance met with the Islamic Development Bank to discuss investment in the energy sector, focusing on the Rogun HPP for energy security and green energy. They also reviewed cooperation in transport infrastructure and education facilities. Both sides affirmed commitment to ongoing dialogue and priority projects for sustainable development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explains How Resource Tax Works and Why It's Necessary
item.description: An official explains why high global commodity prices do not equate to excess profits for mining operations in Uzbekistan. The article details how the resource tax accounts for project costs and ensures normal profitability for investors, covering risks and capital investment.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Leads Uzbekistan Delegation at UN General Assembly 81st Session
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva is heading Uzbekistan's delegation at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. Approximately 130 countries are participating in the session, where the Uzbek delegation listened to speeches from various heads of state during the general debates.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan to Simplify Cargo Transit Through Ports and Corridors
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has initiated public discussion on a draft law to ratify an agreement with Pakistan on transit trade. The accord aims to regulate transit freedom, use of transport corridors and ports, and customs procedures. A special committee will be established to coordinate efforts between the two nations.

item.title: Akmal Jumanazarov Appointed Chairman of Defense Industry Committee
item.description: Akmal Jumanazarov has been appointed as the Chairman of the Defense Industry Committee under the Cabinet of Ministers. Previously, he headed the Technical Regulation Agency since February 2024. Jumanazarov also served as Deputy Minister of Energy and headed a department within the Cabinet of Ministers.

item.title: Bishkek power engineers increase substation capacity ahead of winter
item.description: In Bishkek, the 'Berlik' substation is increasing the capacity of its second transformer from 16 to 25 thousand kilovolt-amperes. The city's electricity network enterprise reported this. Works are being carried out using a cascade method. The modernization of the city's power grids is planned to continue, with capacity increases also foreseen for the 'Kyzyl-Asker' and 'Central-3' substations.

item.title: Kaspersky Lab begins translating products into Kyrgyz language
item.description: Kaspersky Lab has started translating its products and educational platforms into the Kyrgyz language. The company's Managing Director for Central Asia and Mongolia announced this initiative, which includes adapting the CyberABC educational guide. The project, funded this year, aims to improve digital literacy and cybersecurity in Kyrgyzstan without commercial intent.

item.title: Lebedinovka — GES-5 road to be commissioned in one month
item.description: The Lebedinovka — GES-5 highway is scheduled for commissioning in one month. The head of the construction and reconstruction department of the road transport department reported that the object is 95 percent complete. The road connects Bishkek with the northern bypass. Repairs are also nearing completion on the Bishkek — Kant highway.

item.title: Navoiy kindergarten teacher sentenced to over 3 years for child abuse
item.description: A private kindergarten teacher in Navoiy has been sentenced to over three years in prison for beating children. An assistant teacher recorded the abuse on her first day of work. Psychological evaluations confirmed severe trauma and fear in the children.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Addresses UN General Assembly's 81st Session
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov delivered a speech at the general debates of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. He congratulated the newly elected president and emphasized Kyrgyzstan's commitment to dialogue and peaceful conflict resolution, offering mediation services.

item.title: Azerbaijan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan Begin Joint Military Exercises 'Birlik Kuchi - 2026'
item.description: Azerbaijan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan have launched joint military exercises named 'Birlik Kuchi - 2026' at the 'Qizilgaya' training center in Azerbaijan's Karabakh region. The drills involve military personnel, equipment, naval forces, aviation, and drones from all three nations. The primary goal is to enhance joint operational readiness and interoperability.

item.title: EU Agrees to Lift Sanctions on Russian Billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman
item.description: EU member states' permanent representatives have agreed to remove Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from the sanctions list. This decision was part of a three-year extension of the sanctions program. France and Slovakia had reportedly pushed for Usmanov's removal, citing national security and other reasons.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Select Investors for Energy Projects Through Open Competitive Tenders
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reform its energy investment project system, selecting investors through open competitive tenders. The new model will first define future electricity needs, then required generation capacity and infrastructure. Responsibilities will be divided among ministries for forecasting, strategic planning, and market regulation.

item.title: Tashkent tests dedicated lane for micro-mobility on Lutfiy Street
item.description: Tashkent is piloting a 2.4-kilometer dedicated lane for micro-mobility on Lutfiy Street. This initiative aims to separate bicycles, electric scooters, and similar vehicles from car traffic and pedestrian sidewalks, addressing safety and convenience concerns in the growing urban transport landscape.

item.title: Tashkent plans to convert central green space into parking lot, sparking public concern
item.description: Tashkent's city administration plans to convert a 1.3-hectare green space near the National Library into a paid parking lot. While promising new pedestrian paths and green areas, the decision has raised questions among the public regarding the loss of urban green space.

item.title: Uzbekistan launches initiative to reward best proposals for cutting bureaucracy
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched the "Bureaucracy-Free Uzbekistan" initiative, allowing citizens and entrepreneurs to submit proposals for eliminating excessive bureaucratic processes in state institutions. Participants can receive cash rewards of up to 2 million soms for their suggestions. The program aims to reduce state body functions by 30% and streamline business requirements.

item.title: China tests world's first underwater perovskite solar power station
item.description: Chinese scientists have successfully tested the world's first underwater solar power system using perovskite solar cells at a depth of 10 meters in the open sea. The technology is designed to efficiently utilize the limited spectrum of sunlight penetrating underwater. The system achieved nearly 35% energy conversion efficiency in laboratory conditions.

item.title: Tajikistan launches 250 MW solar power station in Asht district
item.description: Tajikistan has commissioned a 250 MW solar power station in the Asht district of the Sughd region. The station, built on 793 hectares, is expected to cover about 40% of the region's electricity needs. The project aims to reduce energy transmission losses and increase electricity generation capacity in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reviews Mid- and Long-Term Fuel and Energy Sector Development Plans
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed plans for the fuel and energy sector's development, focusing on electricity generation and project management. Reforms have increased renewable energy capacity to over 6.3 GW, with solar and wind power contributing significantly. By 2030, Uzbekistan aims for a $300 billion economy and over 41 million people, necessitating accelerated energy capacity growth to meet rising demand.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Austria to Expand Cooperation in Medical Technologies
item.description: Uzbekistan and Austria have agreed to expand their cooperation in medical technologies. Both sides will continue communication between relevant organizations and establish direct partnerships. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Uzbek-Iranian Agricultural Business Forum Opens New Chapter in Cooperation
item.description: An Uzbek-Iranian agricultural business forum was held in Tashkent to expand trade, economic, and investment ties. Discussions covered livestock, veterinary medicine, aquaculture, seed production, and agricultural technology, including drones. The event aimed to foster new projects and partnerships.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sees Decline in Students Studying Abroad
item.description: In the first three months of 2026, 5,862 Uzbek citizens went abroad for education, rising to 7,355 in four months. This marks a significant decrease compared to last year, with 2,600 fewer students studying abroad. Russia remains the most popular destination, followed by South Korea. This trend may reflect the growth of foreign university branches within Uzbekistan and increased overseas study costs.

item.title: China Faces Extreme Weather: Floods and Droughts Hit Amidst Climate Change
item.description: China is experiencing extreme weather conditions, with forecasts predicting an intense rainy season. Since May, the country has been hit by successive waves of floods, including monsoon rains, typhoons, and glacial floods. Provinces like Hunan have reported fatalities and missing persons due to severe flooding, while other regions faced record rainfall and reservoir breaches.

item.title: Toktogul HPP Repairs Three Hydrogenerators in Preparation for Winter
item.description: The Ministry of Energy reports that repairs on three hydrogenerators at the Toktogul Hydropower Plant are underway as part of preparations for the upcoming winter period. The focus is on maintaining generating equipment and infrastructure. Current repairs are being conducted on hydrogenerators G-1, G-2, and G-4, with specific work scheduled for unit G-4 from September 21-26.
